title: M1: Ingestion — webhook capture, hook creation, resource limits
description: Implement the core webhook capture flow: create hooks via API, receive webhooks at /h/{hook_id}, enforce payload size and resource bounds. After this milestone, hookbin is usable — you can create a hook, POST webhooks to it, and they're stored in SQLite. Resource limits (max hooks, max payload, max requests per hook) are enforced from day one.
goals: POST /api/hooks creates a new webhook inbox and returns its ingestion URL
Any HTTP method to /h/{hook_id} captures the full request (method, headers, body, source IP)
Payload size is enforced before storage — oversized requests are rejected with 413
Max hooks limit prevents unbounded growth of hook inboxes
Max requests per hook evicts oldest requests when the limit is reached
All resource bounds come from Config (CLI flags / TOML)

acceptance_criteria.when: creating a hook via POST /api/hooks and then POSTing a webhook to /h/{hook_id}
acceptance_criteria.then: the webhook is captured and stored in SQLite with all metadata
the server rejects with 413 and a structured error with suggestion

acceptance_criteria.given: a running hookbin server at --max-hooks limit
acceptance_criteria.then: the server rejects with a structured error
